newsitem.title: USA: Cyrix unveils new chip, shares jump.
newsitem.headline: Cyrix unveils new chip, shares jump.

text.p: Shares of Cyrix Corp jumped about 18 percent after the chipmaker unveiled a processor that will compete with Intel Corp's Pentium II at half the price.

Cyrix, one of the few technology issues that showed gains on Friday, rallied four points to 26 in heavy trading. By mid-afternoon, about 8.1 million shares changed hands, which is about 10 times Cyrix's normal trading volume.
Cyrix's new 6x86MX processor, formerly code-named M2, is the Richardson, Texas-based firm's latest challenge to Intel's domination of the PC industry.

"The 6x86MX processor now enables our customers to deliver high-performance, MMX-enabled entertainment PCs in the rapidly growing sub-$1,500 category. Our entire product line offers the best price/performance value in the industry," said Jay Swent, acting Cyrix chief executive.
International Business Machines Corp said Friday it will manufacture Cyrix's new chip and will market an IBM-branded version.

Cyrix's announcement Friday fired another blow at rival Intel. Shares of Intel sank sharply Friday after the leading maker of comuter chips said its second quarter revenue and profit will fall short of expectations.
Intel dropped 13-9/64 to 150-5/8 in afternoon trading, recovering from a morning low of 140.
